about.title: About · Supaporn Klabklaydee | Ph.D. Researcher · Institute of Science Tokyo
about.desc: About Supaporn Klabklaydee (Boat) — Ph.D. student at Institute of Science Tokyo. Background in environmental engineering, cheminformatics, and machine learning for ecotoxicity prediction.
about.heroSubHtml:
Ph.D. Student · Environmental Chemistry & Cheminformatics · Institute of Science Tokyo · Fujii Lab
GNN · Molecular graphs · Ecotoxicity · PFAS · DOM
about.hubDesc: From published GSAT benchmarks to the in-progress CRAM thesis — dive into molecular graphs, toxicity, and biotransformation.
about.affilHtml:
Ph.D. Student · Civil & Environmental Engineering
Institute of Science Tokyo · Fujii Lab
about.bio1Html: I am a Ph.D. student in Civil and Environmental Engineering at the Institute of Science Tokyo, supervised by Prof. Manabu Fujii (Fujii Lab). My doctoral research focuses on AI-Driven Generation of Carboxyl-Rich Aliphatic/Alicyclic Molecules (CRAM) — a property-conditioned deep learning approach for understanding refractory dissolved organic matter — alongside developing the CRAM-GTransformer, a bidirectional graph transformer for site-specific and pathway-level CRAM biotransformation prediction.
about.bio2Html: With extensive experience in data analysis using Python, R, and Julia, I am passionate about leveraging AI to solve complex environmental challenges — from PFAS contamination and marine carbon cycling to biotransformation pathway prediction and kinetic modeling.
about.bio3Html: Beyond models, I care about reproducible scientific software: SLURM/GPU pipelines, containerized workflows, and tools other labs can actually run. Collaborations span JAMSTEC, RIKEN, and LLNL DSSI 2025. I am based in Yokohama/Tokyo and open to joint projects, internships, and invited talks.
about.currentNote: Open to new collaborations — click any topic to learn more. Research interests also span other pages of this site.

research.title: Research · Supaporn Klabklaydee | GNN Ecotoxicity · Environmental Informatics
research.desc: Research by Supaporn Klabklaydee: GNN-based LC50 prediction, GSAT attention model, aquatic toxicology, transformation products, and water quality informatics.
research.heroSub: Computational Environmental Science · Machine Learning · Molecular Discovery
research.introHtml: My work sits at the intersection of environmental engineering, computational chemistry, and deep learning. I build models and pipelines that help us understand how pollutants transform, persist, and interact in complex environmental systems.
research.collabNote: I am actively open to new collaborations — click any topic to learn more and reach out.
research.c1Desc: Decoding dissolved organic matter structural complexity in aquatic environments using HR-MS/MS and generative models.
research.c2Desc: Multigenerational toxicity prediction using Graph Neural Networks and Graph Transformers for environmental pollutant risk assessment.
research.c3Desc: High-throughput profiling of unknown PFAS transformation products to elucidate degradation pathways in the environment.
research.c4Desc: Large-scale discovery of novel marine enzymes using protein language models and deep clustering of ocean sequence space.
research.c5Desc: Physics-informed and graph-based models for environmental persistence, half-lives, and reaction dynamics across depth.
research.c6Desc: Molecular formula assignment, isomer expansion, and chemical space navigation for complex environmental mixtures.
research.c7Desc: SHAP and attribution methods that make GNN toxicity predictions interpretable for chemists and regulators.
